title: Tularosa Basin Downwinders Consortium
summary: A New Mexico advocacy group co-founded in 2005 by Fred Tyler and Tina Cordova. It campaigns for recognition of, and compensation for, people it says were harmed by fallout from the 16 July 1945 Trinity test, and presses Congress to extend the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act to New Mexico.

uncertainty.note: End year 2021 is only the latest date at which a source opened shows the group active; no dissolution is recorded and the group continues.

as_recorded.value: It was co-founded in 2005 by Fred Tyler and Tina Cordova
working for 16 years to bring attention to the negative health effects

where.modern_name: Tularosa Basin, south-central New Mexico, USA (pin at the Trinity Site; the group is headquartered in Albuquerque)
where.historical_name: Tularosa Basin and Trinity Site area, New Mexico, United States

importance.justification: Leading advocacy organization for civilians exposed to fallout from the first nuclear test, central to the push to extend RECA to New Mexico.

audience_note: Discusses civilians who say they were harmed by radioactive fallout, including cancer deaths. Health claims are the group's own and are not independently verified here.
